days.heading: 06 JUNE | DELHI TO AYODHYA
days.body: Assistance at Ayodhya airport. Ayodhya is an ancient, sacred city in Uttar Pradesh, India, revered as the birthplace of Lord Rama, the central figure of the Ramayana, and a major Hindu pilgrimage site situated on the Saryu River. Formerly the capital of the ancient Kosala Kingdom and Oudh State, it's now a rapidly developing tourist hub, famous for the newly built Ram Mandir at the Rama Janmabhoomi site, attracting millions of devotees and visitors. Upon arrival, transfer to the hotel. In the evening, we will go for sightseeing Ram Mandir, Shri Hanuman Garhi Mandir, Kanak Bhawan, Dashrath Marg and Saryu River etc. Return to the hotel for overnight stay.

days.heading: 07 JUNE | AYODHYA TO VARANASI (219 KMS / 4H 15M)
days.body: After breakfast from the hotel, we will drive to Varanasi. Varanasi, also known as Kashi or Banaras, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world and holds immense spiritual, cultural, and historical significance. Located on the banks of the sacred River Ganga in Uttar Pradesh, India, Varanasi is regarded as the spiritual capital of India. The city is famous for its ghats, where pilgrims perform rituals, take holy dips, and conduct evening Ganga Aarti, a mesmerizing spiritual ceremony. Varanasi is a major centre of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, with nearby Sarnath being the place where Lord Buddha delivered his first sermon. Upon arrival check in & later, we will go to the banks of the Ganges River to witness the evening Aarti ceremony. After the ceremony, return to the hotel and overnight stay.

days.heading: 08 JUNE | IN VARANASI | SARNATH VISIT
days.body: At dawn, we will take a boat ride on the Ganges, where we will observe devotees along the ghats, purifying themselves and making their offerings. After that return to the hotel for breakfast. At the scheduled time, we will continue with a visit to Sarnath, where Buddha delivered his first sermon. We will visit the museum, the remaining stupas, and the garden with a statue of Buddha. Sarnath, near Varanasi, is a profoundly sacred Buddhist pilgrimage site where Gautama Buddha first taught the Dharma, establishing Buddhism after his enlightenment; it features ancient ruins, stupas (like Dhamek Stupa), monasteries, the iconic Ashoka Pillar with the Lion Capital, and the Sarnath Museum, making it a key center for Buddhist art, history, and culture, easily reachable from Varanasi by road or train. After the visit, return to the hotel. Overnight stay.

days.heading: 09 JUNE | DEPARTURE FROM VARANASI
days.body: After breakfast, free time until the transfer to the airport. Boarding of the return flight to Delhi. Arrival and end of services, taking home unforgettable memories of the sacred cities of Ayodhya and Varanasi, renowned for their spiritual heritage, ancient traditions, and riverside beauty, as well as India's rich culture, history, and architecture. “THANK YOU FOR CHOOSING TO EXPLORE WITH US!”

days.heading: DELHI
days.body: Morning after breakfast, discover the timeless charm of Delhi, a city where ancient heritage and modern vibrancy coexist seamlessly. India’s capital offers a rich tapestry of history, culture, and architecture, reflecting centuries of dynasties, empires, and cultural influences. Begin your sightseeing tour in Old Delhi, where narrow lanes, bustling bazaars, and historic landmarks narrate stories of the Mughal era. Visit the iconic Jama Masjid, one of the largest mosques in Asia, followed by a panoramic drive past the majestic Red Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a symbol of India’s rich past. Experience the lively atmosphere of Chandni Chowk, a centuries-old market renowned for its vibrant streets and traditional flavors. Transition to New Delhi, designed during the British era, is characterized by wide boulevards and grand architecture. Drive past the ceremonial Rajpath, India Gate, Parliament House, and the President’s House, showcasing the city’s colonial legacy and administrative grandeur. Explore the elegant Humayun’s Tomb, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a precursor to the Taj Mahal, set amidst beautifully landscaped gardens. Continue to Qutub Minar, the world’s tallest brick minaret and another UNESCO-listed monument, admired for its intricate carvings and historical significance. Depending on time, a visit to the serene Lotus Temple or Akshardham Temple offers a glimpse into Delhi’s spiritual diversity and contemporary architectural brilliance. Overnight stay at a Delhi hotel.

days.heading: DELHI – NEEMRANA – JAIPUR (269Kms, 05Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast, drive to Jaipur en route Neemrana Fort: Perched majestically on the Aravalli Hills, Neemrana Fort Palace is a magnificent 15th-century heritage fort that reflects the grandeur of Rajasthan’s royal legacy. Once the residence of the Chauhan rulers, the fort has been meticulously restored and transformed into a world-class heritage hotel, offering an unforgettable blend of history, luxury, and timeless elegance. Spread across multiple terraced levels, the fort showcases an exquisite fusion of Rajput and Mughal architecture, featuring grand courtyards, regal halls, vintage artifacts, and panoramic views of the surrounding countryside. As you explore the fort, each passage and balcony narrates stories of valor, romance, and royal splendor. Continue drive to Jaipur. Upon arrival, check in at the hotel in Jaipur. Overnight stay at Jaipur hotel.

days.heading: JAIPUR
days.body: Morning Visit the ancient Rajput capital of Amber, located just 11 km from Jaipur, and experience one of Rajasthan’s most magnificent hill forts. Begin your visit with a memorable ascent to the fort (traditionally by elephant ride, subject to availability), offering a regal introduction to this historic stronghold. Constructed in the late 16th century by Raja Man Singh, Amber Fort served as the seat of power for the Rajput rulers until Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II established the new capital at Jaipur. Built in a harmonious blend of Rajput and Mughal architecture, the fort-palace complex is renowned for its grandeur and artistic refinement. Explore the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), the revered Kali Temple, the splendid Jai Mandir or Hall of Victory, celebrated for its intricately inlaid panels and shimmering mirror ceilings, and the cooling Sukh Niwas, designed with a natural water-flow system to provide relief from the summer heat. Perched above Maota Lake, Amber Fort offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding hills and the tranquil waters below, making it one of the most iconic and photogenic landmarks of Rajasthan. Afternoon Enjoy a half-day sightseeing tour of Jaipur, exploring its most iconic landmarks that reflect the city’s royal heritage and scientific brilliance. Begin with a visit to the Maharaja’s City Palace, located within Jaipur’s historic walled city. Built in 1732 AD, this magnificent palace complex occupies nearly one-seventh of the old city and continues to be a symbol of Jaipur’s regal legacy. Explore the elegant Mubarak Mahal, along with its fascinating textile and armoury museums, showcasing royal costumes, weaponry, and artifacts from centuries past. Visit the Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience) and Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), where the rulers once conducted state affairs and public hearings. Continue to the Jantar Mantar Observatory, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the oldest astronomical observatory in India. Meaning “instruments for measuring the harmony of the heavens,” Jantar Mantar features a remarkable collection of large-scale astronomical instruments, each precisely designed to measure time, track celestial bodies, and provide highly accurate astronomical readings. Conclude the tour with a photo stop at the Hawa Mahal (Palace of the Winds), Jaipur’s most recognizable façade, famed for its intricately carved pink sandstone windows. Drive past the city’s distinctive rose-pink residential and commercial areas, offering a glimpse into the vibrant daily life of the Pink City. Overnight stay at Jaipur hotel.

days.heading: JAIPUR – ABHANERI – FATEHPUR SIKRI – AGRA (257Kms, 05Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Agra enroot visiting Abhaneri: Based on stylistic and architectural similarities with the terraced temples of Paranagar and Mandore, historians date Chand Baori to the 8th–9th century, making it an outstanding example of early water architecture in India. Archaeological assessment suggests that the stepwell was likely constructed prior to the adjoining Harshat Mata Temple, underscoring its primary role as a vital water source for the region. Chand Baori is particularly notable for its extraordinary geometric precision and monumental scale, featuring thousands of symmetrically arranged steps descending to the water level. As observed by architectural historian Morna Livingston in Steps to Water: The Ancient Stepwells of India, Chand Baori is one of the rare stepwells that embodies “two classical periods of water building in a single setting,” highlighting its historical continuity and architectural evolution. Today, Chand Baori stands as a remarkable testament to India’s ancient engineering ingenuity, seamlessly blending functionality, spirituality, and aesthetic excellence. Fatehpur Sikri: The magnificent fortified city of Fatehpur Sikri, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was built in 1569 by Emperor Akbar as the capital of his Mughal Empire. Despite its grandeur and meticulous planning, the city was abandoned merely 15 years later, reportedly due to a chronic scarcity of water, earning it the evocative title of a ghost city. As you explore this remarkably preserved complex, visit its most celebrated monuments, including the majestic Jami Masjid, one of the largest mosques of its time; the revered Tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti, crafted in exquisite white marble; the five-storeyed Panch Mahal; and the impressive Diwan-i-Khas, famed for its central pillar and unique architectural design. The tour also includes views of various royal palaces that once formed the heart of Akbar’s courtly life. Fatehpur Sikri stands as a masterpiece of Mughal architecture, where Islamic design principles harmoniously merge with Hindu and Jain decorative elements, reflecting Emperor Akbar’s vision of cultural synthesis. The city remains a powerful testament to a brief yet brilliant chapter in India’s imperial history. Continue drive to Agra. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Agra. Rest of the day free for relaxation. Overnight stay at Agra hotel.

days.heading: AGRA
days.body: Morning after breakfast, proceed for a sightseeing tour of Agra, visiting Taj Mahal: Emperor Shah Jahan, a ruler renowned for his passion for architecture, resolved to create a marble memorial that would endure as one of the world’s most profound expressions of love and artistry. The site was deliberately chosen along a gentle bend of the Yamuna River, allowing the monument to be visible from Shah Jahan’s private chambers within Agra Fort, located further upstream. Construction of the Taj Mahal began in 1631 and spanned 22 years, engaging over 20,000 skilled artisans and craftsmen from across the empire and beyond. The result is a masterpiece that harmoniously balances monumental scale with exquisite detail, where architectural symmetry, refined proportions, and intricate marble inlay converge in perfect unity. The Taj Mahal stands today as a poignant mausoleum that blends subtlety with grandeur—an eternal symbol of devotion, aesthetic brilliance, and the zenith of Mughal architectural achievement. Agra Fort: The construction of Agra Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was initiated in 1565 by Emperor Akbar, marking the rise of Mughal power in northern India. Enclosed by formidable sandstone ramparts stretching over 2.5 kilometers and protected by a deep moat more than 10 metres wide, the fort stands as an imposing symbol of imperial strength and strategic brilliance. Far more than a military stronghold, Agra Fort functioned as a self-contained imperial city, housing palaces, mosques, audience halls, and administrative quarters. Within its walls, visitors encounter architectural masterpieces such as the elegant Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque), the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), and the richly ornamented Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience). The complex also includes the Octagonal Tower, from where Emperor Shah Jahan is believed to have gazed upon the Taj Mahal, as well as Jahangir’s Palace, reflecting a blend of Hindu and Islamic architectural styles. Agra Fort remains a remarkable testament to Mughal architectural ingenuity and royal life, offering profound insights into the empire’s political, cultural, and artistic legacy. Itmad-Ud-Daula: Built in 1622, this exquisite mausoleum was commissioned for Ghiyas Beg, the father of Empress Nur Jahan, wife of Emperor Jahangir. Gracefully crafted in white marble, the tomb is adorned with delicate mosaic work, intricate pietra dura inlay, and fine lattice (jali) screens, reflecting a refined aesthetic that marked a significant transition in Mughal architecture. Often referred to as the “Baby Taj,” the monument is notable as the first Mughal structure to be entirely clad in white marble with contrasting stone inlay, setting an important architectural precedent later perfected in the Taj Mahal. Unlike larger imperial mausoleums, Itimad-ud-Daulah’s Tomb possesses an intimate scale and a tranquil ambiance, offering visitors a sense of gentle serenity and understated elegance. Mehtab Bagh is the last of the eleven Mughal gardens constructed along the Yamuna River, positioned directly opposite the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort, with Ram Bagh being the earliest of these landscaped gardens. Historical records attribute the original creation of this site to Emperor Babur (d. 1530), highlighting its early significance in Mughal garden design. Later, Emperor Shah Jahan identified the crescent-shaped, grass-covered floodplain across the Yamuna as an ideal vantage point for viewing the Taj Mahal. The garden was subsequently developed as a “moonlit pleasure garden,” known as Mehtab Bagh, offering a serene and symmetrical counterpoint to the monument across the river. Designed as an integral component of the Taj Mahal complex, Mehtab Bagh followed the classic Mughal riverfront terrace pattern, with its width precisely matching that of the Taj Mahal itself. The garden once featured white plastered walkways, elegant pavilions, reflective pools, and fountains, planted with fruit trees and fragrant flowers such as narcissus. Today, Mehtab Bagh provides one of the most tranquil and picturesque views of the Taj Mahal, especially at sunset and under moonlight. Overnight stay at Agra hotel.

days.body: Arrival at the airport 3 hours before departure for check-in on a scheduled Turkish Airlines flight to Delhi, with a layover in Istanbul. Overnight flight. Upon arrival, our representative will meet you and take you to the hotel for breakfast and to leave your luggage. Depending on hotel availability, we will either check in immediately or begin our tour of Old Delhi. At the scheduled time, we will visit Old Delhi, including the Jama Masjid mosque (the largest in the country), and stop at the Red Fort, one of the most opulent from the Mughal Empire era. We will take a rickshaw ride through the narrow streets. We will then continue to Raj Ghat (Gandhi's memorial). Afterwards, we will return to the hotel to check in. Dinner and overnight stay..

days.heading: DELHI
days.body: Discover the contrasting charms of India’s capital on this enriching Delhi sightseeing tour. Begin in New Delhi, renowned for its British colonial planning, wide tree-lined avenues, and elegant bungalows. Visit the serene Laxminarayan Temple and the iconic India Gate, the 42-metre-high War Memorial Arch. Enjoy a panoramic drive past the Parliament House, Secretariat buildings, and the former Vice Regal Palace, now the official residence of the President of India. Continue to the impressive Qutab Minar, envisioned as the most magnificent tower of victory and the model for all future minars in India. Your journey then leads to Old Delhi, where history and heritage come alive. Explore the grand 17th-century Jama Masjid, the largest mosque in India, and experience the vibrant atmosphere of Chandni Chowk, the bustling heart of old Delhi’s markets. Drive past the majestic Red Fort for a memorable photo stop before concluding at Raj Ghat, the tranquil memorial marking the cremation site of Mahatma Gandhi. Overnight stay at Delhi hotel.

days.heading: DELHI - AGRA
days.body: In the morning, depart by road for Agra – the city of the Taj Mahal. Upon arrival in Agra, transfer to your hotel. Renowned for being home to one of the Seven Wonders of the World, the Taj Mahal, as well as for its historical monuments, magnificent architecture, and the beauty of its marble, Agra stands out as one of India's main tourist destinations. The city is famous for its marble inlay work, crafted by artisans whose expertise dates back to the Mughal era. Agra's handicrafts also include carpet making, gold embroidery, and leather shoes. After checking into your hotel, visit the Agra Fort. Built during the reign of Akbar, the third Mughal emperor, this imposing fort of red sandstone houses the magnificent Pearl Mosque in white marble, as well as the palaces, halls, courtyards, and fountains built by his sons and successors, Jahangir and Shah Jahan. It was here, in fact, that Shah Jahan spent the last years of his life, imprisoned by his own son, Aurangzeb. Overnight stay at the hotel.

days.heading: AGRA – JAIPUR via Fatehpur Sikri (239Kms / 4h30Mnts)
days.body: On the way to Fatehpur Sikri. Fatehpur Sikri is the former royal city of Emperor Akbar, now deserted. This impressive and remarkably well-preserved citadel became his capital in 1571. Here, you can visit the mosque, designed to accommodate 10,000 worshippers, as well as the palaces, residences, and audience halls, all built of ornamental red sandstone. Akbar left Fatehpur Sikri in 1584 to consolidate his outlying territories, leaving the city as we see it today—in a state of almost perfect preservation. Then, we continue on the road to Jaipur. Jaipur, the capital of the Rajput state of Rajasthan, is famous for its architectural wonders and rich cultural heritage. Adorned with pink sandstone palaces, majestic forts, and lush gardens against the picturesque backdrop of the Aravalli Hills, Jaipur embodies both the charm of India's glorious past and the sophistication of a thriving metropolis. The city was founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, when he decided to move his capital from Amer to Jaipur. A great architect, astronomer, and passionate scientist, he designed his capital with remarkable geometric precision, making Jaipur one of the best-planned cities in India. In the evening, stroll through the famous local Bapu Bazaar, renowned for its colorful textiles, jewelry, and traditional handicrafts. Overnight at the hotel.

days.heading: JAIPUR – PUSHKAR (142Kms / 2h45mnts)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Pushkar. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Pushkar. Afternoon proceed for sightseeing tour of Pushkar. The sacred town of Pushkar is best known for its revered Brahma Temple, a rare shrine that draws pilgrims throughout the year. Beyond its spiritual aura, Pushkar comes alive during the famous Cattle and Camel Fair, held annually in the month of Kartik (October/November). This vibrant festival attracts thousands of visitors from across the world, offering a colourful blend of culture, tradition, and rural charm. Overnight stay at Pushkar hotel

days.heading: PUSHKAR – JODHPUR (189Kms / 3h 33mn)
days.body: After breakfast, depart by road for Jodhpur – the Blue City. In the afternoon, we will visit Mehrangarh Fort and Jaswant Thada. Mehrangarh Fort is a majestic 15th-century fort located in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, built by Rao Jodha on a 120-meter-high hill. Nicknamed the "Citadel of the Sun," it is one of the largest forts in India and a symbol of Rajput royal heritage. The fort is famous for its impressive architecture, housing magnificent palaces, a museum rich in royal artifacts, and thick, imposing walls. It also offers spectacular views of the "Blue City" stretching out below. Overnight stay at the hotel.

days.heading: JODHPUR – UDAIPUR VIA RANAKPUR (249Kms / 5h 15mn)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Udaipur enroot visiting Ranakpur : Located about 90 km from Udaipur, Ranakpur is home to the largest Jain temple complex in India, dating back to the 15th century. The main temple, dedicated to Adinath, the first Tirthankar, is renowned for its breathtaking artistry. Every surface—from walls and domes to ceilings and pillars—is adorned with intricate carvings depicting mythological figures, floral motifs, and geometric patterns. The complex features 1,444 exquisitely carved marble pillars, each one unique, showcasing an extraordinary level of craftsmanship. Please note: Temples open at 1200 hrs. Leather belts, footwear, bare legs, and black clothing are not permitted within the premises. Set amidst the serene Aravalli hills of southern Rajasthan, Udaipur, often called the City of Sunrise, is celebrated as one of India’s most romantic destinations. The city presents a captivating panorama of shimmering lakes, elegant marble palaces, lush gardens and rolling green hills—earning it the enduring title of “The Venice of the East.” Founded in 1568 by Maharana Udai Singh II, Udaipur was conceived as a traditionally planned, fortified city adorned with magnificent palaces, ornate temples and stately havelis. Over the centuries, it also flourished as a thriving centre for performing arts, painting and traditional crafts, nurturing a rich cultural legacy that continues to enchant visitors today. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Udaipur. Rest of the day at leisure. Overnight stay at Udaipur hotel.

days.heading: UDAIPUR
days.body: Begin your half-day sightseeing tour of Udaipur with a visit to the City Palace and Museum, the largest palace complex in India and an exquisite fusion of Mughal and Rajput architectural styles. Continue to the 17th-century Jagdish Temple, an important Hindu shrine known for its stunning carvings and towering shikharas. Drive along the serene shoreline of Fatehsagar Lake before exploring Sahelion ki Bari—the enchanting Garden of the Maids of Honour—adorned with delicately carved marble pavilions, sparkling fountains and lush lotus pools. Conclude your tour with a visit to the Bharatiya Lok Kala Mandir, the Folk Art Museum, which showcases Rajasthan’s vibrant cultural traditions through its rich collection of costumes, masks, puppets and folk artefacts. Afternoon enjoy a serene boat ride on Lake Pichola, a picturesque expanse stretching 4 km in length and 3 km in width, framed by rolling hills, majestic palaces, elegant havelis, ancient ghats, and lakeside temples. As you glide across its tranquil waters, take in unforgettable views of Udaipur’s enchanting skyline. The experience is enhanced with a visit to Jag Mandir Island, renowned for its magnificent Gul Mahal Pavilion, an exquisite symbol of the city’s royal splendour. Overnight at Udaipur hotel

days.heading: UDAIPUR – DELHI (FLIGHT)
days.body: On time transfer to airport to board flight for Delhi. Meeting and assistance at Delhi domestic airport and transfer to hotel. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Delh. Overnight stay at Delhi hotel.

days.heading: DELHI – KATHMANDU (FLIGHT)
days.body: On time transfer to airport to board flight for Kathmandu. Meeting and assistance upon arrival at Kathmandu airport and transfer to hotel. Upon arrival at Tribhuwan International airport Kathmandu, meet and assist by our representative and transfer to hotel. Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal and the largest urban agglomerate of Nepal. The agglomerate consists of Kathmandu Metropolitan City at its core, and its sister cities Patan, Kirtipur, Thimi, and Bhaktapur. It also includes the recently recognized urban areas of Shankhapur, Karyabinayak, Champapur, Banepa, Dhulikhel and Panauti. According to a census conducted in 2011, Kathmandu metropolis alone has 975,453 inhabitants, and the agglomerate has a population of more than 2.5 million inhabitants. The city stands at an elevation of approximately 1,400 meters (4,600 ft) in the bowl-shaped Kathmandu Valley of central Nepal. It is surrounded by four major mountains: Shivapuri, Phulchoki, Nagarjun and Chandragiri. Overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

days.heading: KATHMANDU
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for full day sightseeing tour of Kathmandu visiting Kathmandu Durbar Square: Kathmandu’s number one tourist attraction swarms with life. Though a few of the square’s 50-plus monuments date from the 12th century, most are from the time of the Malla Kings. Probably the most famous building here is the Kumari Bahal, a building richly decorated with beautiful woodcarvings, which is home to the Royal Kumari, the Living Goddess, and a manifestation of the great goddess Durga. Nearby the former Royal Palace is a Mall Dynasty dwelling, once considerably more extensive than today. Within, the courtyard Nassal Chowk, originally hosted dramatic dance performances, now it is the coronation site of the Shah kings and contains some of the finest wood carvings you will see anywhere in the kingdom. The 14th century Jagannath Mandir is the oldest temple in the area, its steps carved with inscriptions in many languages, nearby Taleju Mandir is one of the largest and finest temples in the Valley. Visit Kumari Temple – Living Goddess: Kumari, A ‘living goddess’ made a rare public appearance to take center stage at a religious festival in Nepal.A Kumari, meaning virgin in Nepalese, is a young prepubescent girl, considered by devotees to be incarnations of the Hindu goddess of power, Kali. Swayambhunath: The most ancient and enigmatic of the Valley’s holy shrines the golden-spired stupa of Swayambhunath tops a wooded hillock. Records of its history date as far as the 5th century, but its origins are believed to be older. It is the Kathmandu Valley’s most sacred Buddhist shrine and whilst its worshippers include the Vajrayana Buddhists of northern Nepal and Tibet, Newari Buddhists are the most fervent devotees. Patan: Patan, the ancient city, once a kingdom in itself, is situated across the Bagmati River to the south of Kathmandu. Patan Durbar Square offers the finest display of Newari urban architecture in Nepal. There are temples devoted to Shiva, Krishna, Ganesh and Vishnu all actively visited by residents and visitors. At the northern end of the square the ancient sunken water tap has been restored and is still in use with young girls filling huge jugs from the carved Stone waterspouts. The courtyards of the Royal Palace with their ornamented windows, columned arcades, shrines and sunken royal bath are amongst the loveliest in all Kathmandu. Overnight stay at Kathmandu hotel.

days.heading: KATHMANDU
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for sightseeing tour of Pashupatinath: situated approx. 4 km east of Kathmandu city, Pashupatinath temple is one of the holiest Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. Situated, amidst a lush green natural setting on the bank of the sacred Bagmati River, the temple built in pagoda style has gilted roof and richly carved silver doors. Visitors will be permitted to view the temple from the east bank of river Bagmati, entrance in the temple being strictly forbidden to all non Hindus. Pashupatinath is the centre of annual pilgrimage on the day of Shivratri which falls in the month of February/March. Behind the temple are the cremation grounds. Boudhanath: This stupa, approx. 7 km east of Kathmandu city is one of the biggest in the world of its kind. It stands with four pairs of eyes in the four cardinal direction keeping watch for righteous behavior and human prosperity. This Buddhist stupa was built by King Man Deva at the advice of Goddess Mani Jogini. It is built on an octagonal base inset with prayer wheels. The shrine is ringed by houses of Lamas or Buddhist priests. PM: Sightseeing tour of Bhaktapur Durbar Square along with a heritage walk through its medieval alleys. Visit a Local Family to gain insight into the lifestyle of the locals. Bhaktapur Durbar Square: Bhaktapur lies only at the distance of 13 km to the east from the capital city, Kathmandu, one can have an opportunity to experience a different world, the world full of vibrant cultures, colorful festivals, generations old craftsmanship, and on top of that it is very worthwhile experiencing its indigenous lifestyle – still preserved old houses, still practiced traditional ways of welcoming guests, still practiced culinary & cutlery and many more experiences. As you walk in, you cannot but be overcome by a feeling of inner harmony. Such is the art and architecture and the special layout here. The Palace of 55 Windows built during the period of King Bhupatindra Malla in 1754 situated to the left as you enter through the city gate, inspires admiration. The National Art Gallery is also housed inside. The palace entrance, the Golden Gate known as SunkoDhoka in Nepali is a masterpiece in repousse art. In front of the palace building is a medley of temples of various designs. Amongst the three Durbar Squares in the Valley, the Durbar Square in Bhaktapur is the best preserved one. Overnight at Kathmandu Hotel.

days.heading: RANTHAMBORE
days.body: Morning and afternoon safari at Ranthambore National Park. Ranthambore National Park – A Legendary Wildlife Experience: One of India’s finest and most celebrated tiger reserves, Ranthambore National Park offers an exceptional opportunity to witness the majestic Royal Bengal Tiger in its natural habitat. Visitors staying for a couple of nights significantly enhance their chances of spotting these elusive predators amidst the park’s dramatic landscape. Once the private hunting reserve of the Maharaja of Jaipur, Ranthambore was brought under the Project Tiger scheme in 1972, marking a major step in wildlife conservation in India. Spread over approximately 410 sq km, the park stretches from the easternmost spur of the Aravalli Range to the Vindhya Hills, creating a unique and diverse ecological setting. The park encompasses both the historic Ranthambore Fort and the wildlife sanctuary, with the nearby town of Sawai Madhopur lending its name to the region. The area also features ancient Jain temples adorned with delicate gilded paintings. Beyond tigers, the park supports a rich variety of wildlife. Sightings often include herds of chital (spotted deer) and sambar, sounders of wild boar, along with nilgai antelope and chinkara gazelles. The park is also home to sloth bears, a few leopards, and marsh crocodiles found near lakes and water bodies. Ranthambore is equally renowned for its diverse birdlife, making it a paradise for birdwatchers. Species commonly seen include spurfowl, jungle fowl, partridges, quails, crested serpent eagles, woodpeckers, flycatchers, and various migratory and resident water birds such as storks, ducks, and geese, especially around the lakes and waterholes. days.body: Morning after breakfast, drive to Agra enroot visiting Abhaneri: Located in the village of Abhaneri, Chand Baori is one of India’s most extraordinary and visually striking stepwells. The structure is traditionally believed to be named after Raja Chanda of the Nikumbh dynasty, although no epigraphic evidence has been discovered to conclusively confirm the identity of its patron or the exact circumstances of its construction. Based on stylistic similarities in architectural design and intricate stone carvings with the terraced temples of Paranagar and Mandore, scholars date Chand Baori to the 8th–9th century, making it one of the earliest surviving stepwells in the country. It is widely believed that the stepwell was constructed prior to the adjoining Harshat Mata Temple, further underlining its significance in the region’s early water-management traditions. As noted by architectural historian Morna Livingston in Steps to Water: The Ancient Stepwells of India, Chand Baori is among the rare stepwells that display “two classical periods of water building in a single setting.” With its geometrically precise, descending tiers of steps and imposing depth, the baori stands as a remarkable example of ancient Indian engineering, combining functionality, aesthetics, and spiritual symbolism. Fatehpur Sikri – Akbar’s Abandoned Capital: The magnificent fortified city of Fatehpur Sikri was built by Emperor Akbar in 1569 and served as the Mughal capital for a brief yet glorious period of about 15 years. The city was later abandoned, reportedly due to a severe scarcity of water, leaving behind one of the finest and most remarkably preserved examples of Mughal architecture in India. As you explore this UNESCO World Heritage Site, visit its most graceful and historically significant structures, including the grand Jama Masjid, the revered Tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti, the elegant Panch Mahal, the Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience), and several royal palaces that reflect Akbar’s vision of imperial grandeur. Fatehpur Sikri is particularly renowned for its unique architectural harmony, where Islamic structural design seamlessly blends with Hindu and Jain decorative elements. This fusion of styles, combined with the city’s hauntingly serene atmosphere, makes Fatehpur Sikri a compelling testament to Akbar’s inclusive vision and a timeless jewel of India’s architectural heritage. days.heading: AGRA
days.body: Morning after breakfast, proceed for sightseeing tour of Agra visiting The Taj Mahal – A Timeless Monument of Love: Emperor Shah Jahan, a passionate patron of architecture, resolved to create a marble memorial that the world would never forget. The site was deliberately chosen on a gentle bend of the Yamuna River, allowing the monument to be viewed from Shah Jahan’s personal palace within Agra Fort, located further upstream—an enduring visual link between the emperor and his beloved. Construction of the Taj Mahal began in 1631 and involved the extraordinary efforts of nearly 20,000 skilled artisans, craftsmen, and architects. The project took 22 years to complete, culminating in one of the most poignant and universally admired mausoleums ever created. The Taj Mahal stands as a masterful fusion of grandeur and subtlety, combining a monumental overall design with exquisitely intricate craftsmanship. Every detail—from the flawless symmetry to the delicate marble inlay work—reflects a level of artistic perfection that has secured the Taj Mahal’s place as an eternal symbol of love and one of the greatest architectural achievements in human history. Agra Fort – The Imperial Stronghold of the Mughals: The construction of Agra Fort was initiated by Emperor Akbar in 1565, establishing one of the most formidable and historically significant forts of the Mughal era. Enclosed by massive red sandstone walls stretching over 2.5 kilometers and encircled by a deep moat more than 10 meters wide, the fort stands as a powerful symbol of Mughal authority and architectural brilliance. Often described as a “city within a city,” Agra Fort encompasses an extraordinary collection of palaces, mosques, and audience halls. Key highlights include the elegant Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque), the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), and the richly adorned Diwan- i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience). Visitors also explore the imposing Octagonal Tower (Musamman Burj), Jahangir’s Palace, and several other royal structures that together narrate the grandeur of imperial life. Often regarded as a milestone in Mughal architecture, the monument is celebrated as the first Mughal structure faced entirely in white marble, richly inlaid with contrasting semi- precious stones. Its artistic innovation later influenced the design and craftsmanship of the Taj Mahal. Affectionately known as the “Baby Taj,” the monument is intimate in scale and enveloped in a sense of gentle serenity. Set amidst tranquil gardens along the Yamuna River, Itmad-ud-Daulah’s Tomb offers visitors a quiet, contemplative experience and stands as a timeless testament to elegance, refinement, and architectural evolution in Mughal India. Islamic architectural principles blend seamlessly with Hindu and Jain decorative traditions, creating a distinctive style expressed through carved brackets, columns, geometric patterns, ornamental motifs and richly sculpted details. Chand Baori, Abhaneri – An Architectural Wonder in Stone: Discover the extraordinary Chand Baori at Abhaneri, one of Rajasthan’s most remarkable examples of traditional water architecture. Believed to have been named after Raja Chanda of the Nikumbh dynasty, the origins of the stepwell remain undocumented, as no definitive epigraphic evidence has yet been found regarding its construction or that of the adjoining Harshat Mata Temple. Created in response to Rajasthan’s arid climate and the vital need to conserve and access water, Chand Baori combines remarkable engineering with extraordinary visual symmetry. Its vast geometric composition of precisely aligned steps descending deep into the earth creates an almost mesmerising architectural spectacle, while the surrounding structures and carved elements reflect the artistic traditions of early medieval Rajasthan. Continue drive to Jaipur. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Jaipur. Jaipur – The Pink City of Royal Grandeur: Founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, Jaipur, popularly known as the “Pink City,” is a remarkable blend of royal heritage, architectural brilliance and meticulous urban planning. Conceived as one of India's earliest planned cities, Jaipur was designed according to the principles of the ancient Shilpa Shastra, with the city divided into nine rectangular sectors, symbolically representing the nine divisions of the universe. The city's master plan was shaped by the vision of its architects, who combined traditional Hindu principles of architecture with the refined influences of Mughal and Jain design, creating a distinctive architectural identity that continues to define Jaipur today. Broad avenues, orderly streets, grand gateways and beautifully ornamented buildings reflect the extraordinary foresight behind its creation. In 1853, the city was famously painted in its characteristic terracotta-pink colour to welcome Prince Albert, who was visiting Jaipur as part of his tour of India. The colour was subsequently preserved as a symbol of hospitality and has become inseparable from the city's identity. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Jaipur.

days.heading: MUNNAR
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for sightseeing tour of Munnar visiting Attukad Waterfalls – A Hidden Gem Amidst Munnar’s Green Hills : Discover the enchanting Attukad Waterfalls, located along the scenic Munnar–Pallivasal road, where cascading water descends gracefully through the verdant hills, resembling a delicate thread of pearls falling from the mountainside. Surrounded by rolling slopes, lush vegetation, and mist-covered landscapes, the falls offer a wonderfully serene setting and an excellent opportunity for photography. The journey to the waterfall is part of the experience. Cross a charming narrow wooden bridge, which is often enveloped in the cool mountain mist, before arriving at this picturesque natural retreat. Along the way, the surrounding forests and vegetation provide opportunities to observe a variety of fascinating flora and fauna native to the Western Ghats. A visit to Attukad Waterfalls is a delightful escape into nature, where mist, flowing water, lush forests, and rolling mountain scenery combine to create one of Munnar’s most picturesque and refreshing experiences Munnar Rose Garden – A Floral Retreat Amidst the Hills: Set amidst the verdant landscapes of Munnar, close to the Kannan Devan Hills Tea Estates and the tranquil Muthirappuzha River, the Munnar Rose Garden forms part of the Sylvan Hill Resort and offers a delightful escape into nature. Spread across beautifully landscaped lawns and gardens, the garden is adorned with colourful blooms, charming animal sculptures, artificial waterfalls and a small aquarium, creating a picturesque setting for a leisurely visit. Stroll through the vibrant gardens and admire an enchanting collection of fresh flowers, while the cool mountain air and peaceful surroundings add to the experience. The garden also offers a variety of recreational activities, including nature walks, trekking, bird watching, boating, badminton and roller skating, making it an enjoyable stop for visitors of all ages. Mattupetty Dam & Lake – Serenity Amidst Munnar’s Hills: Set amidst the picturesque highlands of Munnar, Mattupetty Dam and Lake are among the region’s most popular attractions, inviting visitors to slow down and enjoy the tranquil beauty of the surrounding landscape. Built in the late 1940s, the concrete gravity dam was developed for water conservation, hydroelectric power generation and irrigation, creating the scenic reservoir now known as Mattupetty Lake. Surrounded by rolling green hills, tea plantations and lush vegetation, the lake provides a wonderfully peaceful setting to appreciate Munnar’s natural beauty. Its calm waters mirror the surrounding landscape, creating a particularly picturesque atmosphere that is ideal for photography and moments of quiet relaxation. days.body: Attukad Waterfalls – A Cascading Jewel of Munnar: Tucked away between Munnar and Pallivasal, Attukad Waterfalls is a captivating natural retreat where cascading waters, forested slopes, and rugged mountain landscapes come together in remarkable harmony. Surrounded by undulating terrain and dense greenery, the waterfall offers a refreshing escape into the quieter side of Munnar and is a favourite among both visitors and locals. The journey to Attukad is part of the experience, with the route leading through scenic landscapes and across a charming narrow bridge. From a distance, the waterfall appears like a delicate silver ribbon descending through the emerald hills; as you approach, its true grandeur unfolds as the waters tumble dramatically down the rocky slopes. The waterfall is particularly spectacular during the monsoon season, when the surrounding landscape turns lush and vibrant and the cascading waters gather greater strength. The area also offers opportunities for nature walks, trekking, and hiking, allowing outdoor enthusiasts to appreciate the surrounding wilderness at a leisurely pace. Overnight stay in Munnar

days.heading: ARRIVE DELHI
days.body: Meeting and assistance upon arrival at Delhi International Airport transfer to hotel in Delhi. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Delhi. Delhi – Where Centuries of History Meet the Pulse of Modern India: Few capital cities in the world possess a history as rich, captivating, and enduring as Delhi, the timeless capital of India. For over a millennium, this legendary city has stood at the crossroads of empires, drawing successive dynasties—including the Mongols, Turks, Persians, Afghans, Mughals, and the British—each leaving behind an extraordinary architectural, cultural, and historical legacy that continues to define the city's unique character. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Delhi

days.heading: DELHI
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for Delhi Sightseeing – A Journey Through the Capital’s Heritage The experience then takes you into the vibrant heart of Old Delhi, beginning with a visit to the historic Jama Masjid, commissioned in the 17th century by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Its impressive courtyards, soaring minarets, and red sandstone and marble architecture make it one of the finest examples of Mughal religious architecture in the city. Continue to Chandni Chowk, the historic commercial heart of Old Delhi, where narrow lanes, colourful markets, traditional shops, street-food stalls, and the lively rhythm of everyday life create an unmistakably authentic Delhi experience. A drive past the magnificent Red Fort, with a brief photo stop, offers a glimpse of another great symbol of the Mughal era. Conclude the sightseeing at Raj Ghat, the serene memorial marking the cremation site of Mahatma Gandhi. Set amidst peaceful landscaped gardens, it provides a quiet and reflective conclusion to a day spent discovering Delhi’s remarkable history and heritage Afternoon proceed for an astonishing and beautiful fountain show at Akshardha Temple Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Delhi

days.heading: DELHI – VARANASI (6E 2361 – 12:55HRS / 14:20HRS)
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed to airport to board flight for Varanasi. Meeting and assistance upon arrival at Varanasi airport and transfer to hotel in Varanasi. Varanasi – The Eternal City on the Sacred Ganges: Varanasi, also known as Benares or Kashi, is one of India’s most spiritually evocative cities and one of Hinduism’s seven sacred cities. Set gracefully along the banks of the holy River Ganges, Varanasi is a place where faith, tradition, ritual, and everyday life have intertwined for centuries. It is a city that cannot truly be captured in words—it is best experienced through its atmosphere, sounds, colours, and timeless rituals. With more than a hundred historic ghats lining the Ganges, each carrying its own character and significance, the riverfront forms the spiritual heart of the city. At dawn, the ghats come alive as pilgrims gather for prayers and rituals, while boats glide quietly across the river, offering an unforgettable perspective of the ancient city awakening with the first light of day. Evening witness Ganga Aarti – A Sacred Celebration of Life and Devotion: The Ganga Aarti is far more than a traditional religious ceremony; it is a deeply moving communal experience through which devotees express reverence, gratitude, and devotion to the sacred River Ganges. As evening descends upon the ghats of Varanasi, the riverfront comes alive with the glow of ceremonial lamps, devotional chants, incense, and the rhythmic sound of bells, creating an atmosphere that is both vibrant and profoundly spiritual. One of the most beautiful moments comes when devotees and visitors release small floating lamps, or diyas, onto the river. Each glowing lamp carries a personal prayer, heartfelt wish, or expression of gratitude, gently drifting across the waters and transforming the Ganges into a shimmering stream of light. The simple act creates a powerful connection between the individual, the sacred river, and the timeless traditions of Hindu spirituality. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Varanasi

days.heading: VARANASI – KHAJURAHO (VANDE BHARAT EXPRESSS – 05:15Hrs / 13:10Hrs)

Khajuraho – A Masterpiece of Art, Architecture & Human Expression: The magnificent temples of Khajuraho, built under the patronage of the Chandela dynasty between the 10th and 11th centuries, stand among India’s most extraordinary expressions of medieval architecture, sculpture, and artistic imagination. Once part of a much larger temple complex, the surviving group of temples today offers a remarkable window into the cultural, spiritual, and artistic sophistication of Central India during the Chandela period. Adorned with an astonishing array of finely sculpted figures and intricate ornamental details, the temples portray the many dimensions of human existence—from devotion, music, dance, and everyday life to love and sensuality. The celebrated erotic sculptures, found among the wider repertoire of carvings, have attracted considerable attention and interpretation since the temples were brought to wider international notice following their rediscovery by British officer T. S. Burt in 1838. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Khajuraho

days.heading: KHAJURAHO – ORCHHA (173Kms, 02Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drove to Orchha. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Orchha. Orchha – A Timeless Legacy of the Bundelas: Located approximately 26 km from Jhansi, Orchha is a captivating medieval town founded in 1531 by the Bundela rulers on the serene banks of the Betwa River. Remarkably untouched by the passage of time, Orchha preserves an exceptional collection of magnificent palaces, temples and monuments dating primarily from the 16th and 17th centuries, offering a fascinating glimpse into the grandeur and heritage of medieval India. The town is perhaps best experienced through its impressive fort-palace complex, where imposing stone walls enclose a remarkable world of courtyards, gardens, gateways, pavilions and temples. Rising above the complex are elegant chhatris (cenotaphs) and richly ornamented battlements, creating an enchanting silhouette against the surrounding landscape. The harmonious blend of Rajput architectural traditions, Mughal influences and intricate artistic detailing gives Orchha a distinctive character found nowhere else. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Orchha

days.heading: ORCHHA – JHANSI (17Kms, 43Mnts drive) – AGRA CANTT (VANDE BHARAT EXPRESS

Agra – Where History, Legend & Imperial Grandeur Converge: Situated gracefully on the banks of the Yamuna River, Agra is a city where centuries of history, legend and imperial splendour come together. Tradition attributes the foundation of the present city to Raja Badal Singh around 1475 AD, although references to Agraban in the Mahabharata suggest that the region has enjoyed significance since ancient times and was closely associated with Mathura, one of the oldest sacred cities of northern India. Agra rose to greater prominence during the rule of the Lodi dynasty, when Sikandar Lodi established it as his capital in the late 15th century, laying the foundations for its emergence as an important political and cultural centre of North India. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Agra

days.heading: AGRA – FATEHPUR SIKRI – RANTHAMBORE (308Kms, 05Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Ranthambore enroot visiting Fatehpur Sikri – Akbar’s Vision in Stone What makes Fatehpur Sikri particularly remarkable is the way its architecture reflects the cultural synthesis of Akbar's reign. Islamic architectural principles blend seamlessly with Hindu and Jain decorative traditions, creating a distinctive style expressed through carved brackets, columns, geometric patterns, ornamental motifs and richly sculpted details. Continue drive to Ranthambore. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Ranthambore. Ranthambore – Where Wilderness Meets Royal Heritage: Discover Ranthambore National Park, one of India's most celebrated tiger reserves and a captivating destination where untamed wilderness meets a remarkable royal past. Formerly the private hunting reserve of the Maharajas of Jaipur, the area became part of Project Tiger in 1972, marking an important chapter in India's efforts to protect its magnificent Bengal tiger population. Spread across approximately 410 square kilometres, the reserve occupies a dramatic landscape where the easternmost reaches of the Aravalli Hills meet the Vindhya Range. Ancient rocky outcrops, dry deciduous forests, open grasslands and tranquil lakes create an exceptional habitat for wildlife and provide a spectacular setting for exploration. Ranthambore is particularly renowned for its Bengal tigers, and visitors staying for a couple of nights have a rewarding opportunity to encounter these magnificent animals in their natural surroundings. Alongside the tiger, the park is home to a rich variety of wildlife, including leopards, sloth bears, sambar, spotted deer, wild boar, nilgai, crocodiles and numerous species of birds. Lunch, Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Ranthambore.

Udaipur – The Romantic Soul of Rajasthan: Nestled amidst the undulating Aravalli Hills of southern Rajasthan, Udaipur is one of India's most enchanting cities and is widely regarded as one of the country's most romantic destinations. With its shimmering lakes, magnificent marble palaces, beautifully landscaped gardens and lush green hills, the city presents a picture of timeless elegance and has earned the evocative title of “Venice of the East.” Founded by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1568, Udaipur was conceived as a traditionally planned and fortified city, with imposing palaces, ornate temples, elegant havelis and defensive structures woven into its landscape. The city's architecture reflects the grandeur and sophistication of the Mewar dynasty, while its lakes and surrounding hills lend it an unmistakable sense of tranquillity. Rest of the day free for relaxation / explore surrounding. Dinner and overnight stay at hotel in Udaipur

days.heading: UDAIPUR
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for sightseeing tour of Udaipur City Tour – Palaces, Temples & Artistic Heritage: Begin your half-day sightseeing tour of Udaipur with a visit to the magnificent City Palace and Museum, an extraordinary complex rising majestically above the shores of Lake Pichola. Considered one of the largest palace complexes in India, it represents a harmonious fusion of Rajput architectural traditions and Mughal influences. Explore its ornate courtyards, grand halls, balconies and richly decorated chambers, while the museum offers fascinating insights into the splendour and lifestyle of the former Mewar rulers. Continue to the beautiful Jagdish Temple, an impressive 17th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Its towering structure and intricate stone carvings make it one of Udaipur's most significant religious and architectural landmarks. Take a scenic drive around Fateh Sagar Lake, one of Udaipur's most picturesque lakes, framed by the Aravalli Hills and surrounded by a tranquil landscape. The drive offers wonderful views of the water and the city's elegant lakeside setting. Visit Saheliyon-ki-Bari, meaning the “Garden of the Maids of Honour,” a graceful ornamental garden created as a retreat for the royal ladies. Beautiful fountains, marble kiosks, lotus pools, manicured lawns and shady walkways create an atmosphere of serenity and refinement, offering a glimpse into the leisure and elegance of the Mewar court. Conclude the sightseeing with a visit to the Bharatiya Lok Kala Mandal, also known as the Folk Art Museum, where an engaging collection of traditional Rajasthani folk art, costumes, puppets, masks, musical instruments and decorative crafts celebrates the vibrant cultural traditions of the region. Afternoon enjoy boat ride at Lake Pichola & Jag Mandir – Udaipur’s Timeless Lakeside Beauty: Enjoy a leisurely boat ride on the enchanting Lake Pichola, one of Udaipur's most iconic and picturesque landmarks. Stretching approximately 4 km in length and 3 km in width, the lake is surrounded by the dramatic Aravalli Hills and beautifully framed by magnificent palaces, historic havelis, ancient temples, ghats and elegant embankments. As the boat glides across the tranquil waters, enjoy spectacular panoramic views of Udaipur's architectural treasures reflected against the shimmering surface of the lake. The changing light of the day lends an especially magical character to the landscape, with the palaces and surrounding hills taking on warm golden hues around sunset. Continue to Jag Mandir, a graceful island palace rising from the waters of Lake Pichola. Explore its elegant courtyards, marble structures and beautifully landscaped surroundings, including the exquisite Gul Mahal Pavilion, admired for its refined architecture and historical significance. The experience offers a wonderful opportunity to appreciate Udaipur from a different perspective, where water, architecture, nature and royal heritage come together in perfect harmony. Dinner and overnight stay at hotel in Udaipur

days.heading: UDAIPUR – RANAKPUR – JODHPUR (262Kms, 05Hrs drive)
days.body: Continue drive to Jodhpur. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Jodhpur. Jodhpur – The Blue City at the Gateway to the Thar: Standing proudly at the threshold of the Thar Desert, Jodhpur is the second-largest city in Rajasthan and the historic heart of the Marwar region. Founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha, the city grew into an important centre of Rajput power and commerce, its remarkable heritage still visible throughout its historic streets and monumental architecture. The old city is enclosed by an impressive 10-kilometre-long defensive wall, with ancient gateways leading into a maze of narrow lanes, bustling bazaars and traditional houses. Dominating the city from its dramatic rocky hilltop is the magnificent Mehrangarh Fort, one of Rajasthan's most spectacular fortresses. Its massive ramparts rise above the blue-painted houses below, while the exquisite red-sandstone palaces within form an extraordinary architectural ensemble of courtyards, balconies and richly ornamented interiors. Dinner and overnight stay at hotel in Jodhpur

days.heading: JODHPUR – POKHARAN – JAISALMER (288Kms, 04Hrs drive)
days.body: After sightseeing drive to Jaisalmer enroot visting Pokhran Fort, also known as Balagarh Fort, a distinguished Rajput stronghold rising amidst the stark and captivating landscapes of the Thar Desert. Built in the 14th century by Rao Maldeo, the fort is an impressive example of traditional Rajput architecture, characterised by its imposing sandstone walls, fortified gateways and finely carved architectural details. Constructed as both a fortress and royal residence, Pokhran Fort reflects the remarkable ability of Rajput architects to combine military strength with the elegance and comforts of royal living. Its architecture was thoughtfully adapted to the demanding desert environment, with carefully planned courtyards, shaded spaces and thick sandstone walls providing protection from the harsh climate. Continue drive to Jaisalmer. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Jaisalmer. Jaisalmer – The Golden City of the Thar: Rising majestically from the heart of the Thar Desert, the captivating city of Jaisalmer was founded in 1156 AD by Prince Jaisal, a Rajput ruler of the Bhati dynasty. Built almost entirely from warm yellow sandstone, the city takes on a magical golden hue at sunset, earning it the evocative title of the “Golden City.” Dominating the desert horizon is the magnificent Jaisalmer Fort, with its imposing crenellated walls and labyrinth of narrow lanes leading through a living medieval city. Within and around the fort, exquisitely carved sandstone havelis, ornate façades, temples and traditional residences reveal the extraordinary craftsmanship of the local artisans. Rest of the day free for relaxation / explore surrounding. Dinner and overnight stay at hotel in Jaisalmer

days.heading: JAISALMER (288Kms, 04Hrs drive)
days.body: Also admire Salim Singh Ki Haveli, distinguished by its distinctive architecture and ornate upper storeys, and Nathmalji Ki Haveli, celebrated for its elaborate carvings and remarkable craftsmanship. Together, these mansions reveal the extraordinary skill and imagination of Jaisalmer's master stone craftsmen. As the golden sandstone catches the changing light of the desert sun, the city seems to glow from within, creating an atmosphere that is both timeless and captivating. Afternoon proceed for Osian – An Ancient Oasis of Temple Art & Desert Heritage: Rising gracefully from the golden sands of the Thar Desert, the ancient town of Osian was once an important trading centre between the 8th and 12th centuries, flourishing along the historic caravan routes that connected Rajasthan with distant lands. A visit to Osian is beautifully complemented by a camel safari at sunset. As the sun descends over the endless dunes, casting a warm golden glow across the desert, the slow rhythmic journey by camel offers an evocative and unforgettable experience of Rajasthan’s timeless desert charm. Dinner and overnight stay at hotel in Jaisalmer

days.heading: JAISALMER – BIKANER (330Kms, 05Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Bikaner. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Bikaner. Bikaner – A Desert Legacy of Forts, Havelis & Camels: Set amidst the golden landscapes of northern Rajasthan, Bikaner was founded in 1488 by Rao Bika, son of Rao Jodha, the illustrious founder of Jodhpur. Strategically positioned along the historic caravan routes crossing the Thar Desert, the city grew into an important staging post for traders and travellers journeying between the great desert kingdoms and distant markets. Like many historic cities of Rajasthan, Bikaner’s old quarter is enclosed within impressive crenellated walls, preserving an atmosphere of a bygone era. Wandering through its narrow lanes reveals a captivating ensemble of exquisitely carved merchant havelis, ancient temples and colourful bazaars, where centuries-old traditions continue to lend the city its distinctive medieval character. Evening enjoy visit to local bazaar / explore surrounding. Dinner and overnight stay at hotel in Bikaner

days.heading: BIKANER – DELHI (SSAH DURONT – 12:10Hrs / 19:30Hrs) – DEPART DELHI

days.heading: DELHI – BHUBANESHWAR (6E 2296 : 0920HRS / 1130HRS) – PURI (70KMS, 01 HRS DRIVE)

Later in the afternoon visit World famous temple Jagannath Temple, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Jagannath, a form of Vishnu. The temple is renowned for its annual Ratha Yatra, chariot festival, which honours the three deities - Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra. During the festival, the three principal deities are pulled on large and elaborately decorated raths, or temple cars. The worship is performed by the Bhil Sabar tribal priests, as well as priests of other communities in the temple. Unlike the stone or metal icons found in most Hindu temples, the image of Jagannath is carved from margosa wood and is ceremoniously replaced every 12 or 19 years with an identical replica, with an elaborate month long ceremony called nabakalebar. The temple is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites Dinner overnight stay in Puri

days.heading: PURI – KONARK – PURI (38KMS, 01HRS DRIVE ONE WAY)
days.body: Chandrabagha Beach: According to another ancient narrative reference, Chandrabhag, the daughter of a sage, caught the attraction of the Sun God by her magical charm. The God came down to seek her hand in love. Chandrabhaga did not offer herself to the God. Maddened by romantic pangs, the God chased after a frightened Chandrabhaga, who jumped into the river and killed herself, thus succeeding in protecting her chastity. As a mark of tribute to her sacrifice, every year on the 7th day of the full-moon fortnight of Magha month, people from all over the state and outside gather to take a holy dip in the river that is reduced to a shallow pool, to offer their prayers to the Sun God and to enjoy the sunrise. Konark Sun Temple: The Sun Temple at Konârak, located on the eastern shores of the Indian subcontinent, is one of the outstanding examples of temple architecture and art as revealed in its conception, scale and proportion, and in the sublime narrative strength of its sculptural embellishment. It is an outstanding testimony to the 13th-century kingdom of Orissa and a monumental example of the personification of divinity, thus forming an invaluable link in the history of the diffusion of the cult of Surya,the Sun God. In this sense, it is directly and materially linked to Brahmanism and tantricbelief systems. The Sun Temple is the culmination of Kalingan temple architecture, with all its defining elements in complete and perfect form. A masterpiece of creative genius in both conception and realisation, the temple represents a chariot of the Sun God, with twelve pairs of wheels drawn by seven horses evoking its movement across the heavens. It is embellished with sophisticated and refined iconographical depictions of contemporary life and activities. After visit return back to hotel in Puri. Dinner & overnight stay Puri

days.heading: PURI – BHUBANESHWAR (67KMS, 01HRS DRIVE)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to to Bhubaneshwar enroot visiting Sakshigopal Temple: It is said that a poor young man of the village, later named Sakshigopala, fell in love with the daughter of the village headman. However, being of a higher economic status, the headman opposed marriage between this young man and his daughter. The villagers, including the headman and the young man, went on a pilgrimage to Vrindavan. The village headman fell ill and was abandoned by fellow villagers. The young man tended to him so well that he soon got well, and, in gratitude, promised his daughter in marriage to the young man. As soon as they returned to the village, the headman went back on his promise, asking the young man to produce a witness in support of his claim. Pipi applique market : The Pipli Applique Market, located in the small town of Pipili (Odisha, India), is a vibrant hub famous for traditional "Chandua" patchwork. Hundreds of artisan families craft and sell colorful textiles, wall hangings, and ceremonial umbrellas. Prices are highly affordable, ranging from $2 for small souvenirs to $48 for large, elaborate tapestries. Continue drive to Bhubaneshwar. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Bhubaneshwar. Afternoon visit Kalabhomi craft museum: The museum celebrates the craftsmanship of Odia artisans by putting on display their breath-taking masterpieces. Divided into 2 blocks, the museum has a display area and a live section. The display area focuses on galleries about Handicrafts and Handlooms from around the state while the live section is equipped with an open air theatre as well as separate workshop zones. Kala Bhoomi is built using local raw materials such as the laterite stone which can still be seen in some of the oldest monuments around the state. At Kala Bhoomi we have 10 galleries out of which 9 are open to the public. There are two blocks. The Handicrafts block contains Terracotta, Traditional Paintings, Stone and Wood Carving and Natural Material crafts galleries on the other hand the Handloom block displayed the Pre-Weaving Techniques, Tribal Crafts, The Crafts of Shree Jagannath Culture and Handloom galleries which represents the unique and antique raw materials and equipment as well as variety of Handlooms from across the state. Dinner & overnight stay in Bhubaneshwar

days.body: Morning after breakfast drop at Bhubaneshwar airport to board flight for Kolkata. Meeting and assistance upon arrival at Kolkata airport and transfer to hotel in Kolkata. Upon arrival check in at hotel. Afternoon visit Victoria Memorial: The Victoria Memorial is a large marble monument in the Maidan in Central Kolkata (Calcutta), having its entrance on the Queen's Way. It was built between 1906 and 1921 by the British Raj. It is dedicated to the memory of Queen Victoria, the Empress of India from 1876 to 1901. The work of construction was entrusted to Martin & Co. of Calcutta founded by Rajendranath Mukherjee and Thomas Acquin Martin, and work on the superstructure began in 1910. It is the largest monument to a monarch anywhere in the world. It stands at 26 hectares (64 acres) of gardens and is now a museum under the control of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. Possessing prominent features of the Indo-Saracenic architecture, it has evolved into one of the most popular attractions in the city. Kalighat Temple, dedicated to the Hindu goddess Kali, one of the 10 Mahavidyas in the Hindu tantric tradition and the supreme deity in the Kalikula worship tradition. The temple is one of the 51 Shakti Pithas in India. According to the Devi Bhagavata Purana, Kalika Purana and Shakti Peetha Stotram, the toes of the right foot of Goddess Sati fell here, after Lord Vishnu's Sudarshan Chakra splintered her body into many parts to calm down Mahadev's rage during his cosmic dance. One of the oldest and most important places of worship in Eastern India, being one of the four Adi Shaktipeeth the temple draws hundreds of thousands of devotees throughout the year, especially on occasions like Kali Puja, New Year, Poila Baisakh, Snana Yatra, Durga Puja and the numerous Amavasyas Dinner & overnight stay in Kolkata

days.heading: KOLKATA
days.body: Kapil Muni Aashram: A Gupta era temple existed on this spot. This temple was lost due to coastal erosion. Around the early 19th century, when Warren Hastings had the island cleared of vegetation and the site came under the zamindari of a local Bengali Hindu zamindar from Purba Medinipur called Yaduram who recovered the shrine of Kapilmuni. Then the site came under control of Ramanandi sadhus from Ayodhya. The old temple was made of bamboo which was destroyed in the late 50s or early 60s due to cyclones. The first brick-built temple was built in 1961 for Rs 20,000, and the roof of the temple was made of asbestos. The former Chief Minister Bidhan Chandra Roy contributed Rs 11,000 to the construction of the temple. The construction of the temple was done by "S Chakraborty & Co." The temple was smaller in size than the present temple. Later drive back to hotel in Kolkata. Dinner & overnight stay in Kolkata

days.heading: DEPART KOLKATA (6E 6516 : 1610HRS / 1835HRS)
days.body: Morning after breakfast check out from the hotel and proceed to visit: Jain Temple: The Parshwanath Jain Temple of Kolkata was built by Ray Badridas Bahadur in 1867. Thousands of people visit this temple annually. Parshwanath is actually a complex of 4 temples. The main shrine is dedicated to Shitalanatha, the tenth tirthankara. The pratishtha, or consecration ceremony, was performed by Sri Kalyansurishwarji Maharaj. Three of the temples are dedicated to tirthankars Shitalanatha, Chandraprabha, and Mahavira. The fourth temple is called the Dadawadi and Kushalji Maharaja temple. Footprints of famous Jain monks Acharya Jinadattasuri (1075-1154 CE) and Acharya Jinkushalsuri (born ca. 1280 CE) are installed here. South of the Shitalanatha temple lies the shrine of Chandraprabha, built by Ganeshlal Kapoorchand Jahar in the year 1895. Dakshineshwar Kali Temple: The main temple was inspired by Radhakanta temple in Tollygunge, built by Babu Ramnath Mondal of the Bawali Raj family. The temple compound, apart from the nine-spired main temple, contains a large courtyard surrounding the temple, with rooms along the boundary walls. Along the riverfront, there are twelve shrines dedicated to Shiva, Kali's consort, a temple to Radha–Krishna, a bathing ghat at the river, and a shrine dedicated to Rani Rashmoni. The 'Nahabat', or "music tower," northeast and beyond the last of the Shiva temples, is where Maa Sarada spent a considerable part of her life. Sri Ramakrishna's room is in the northwest corner of the courtyard, with a semicircular verandah facing the river. Belur Math: In the beginning of 1897, Swami Vivekananda arrived at Baranagar, Calcutta with his small group of Western disciples. Two monasteries were founded by him, one at Belur, which became the headquarters of Ramakrishna Mission and the other at Mayavati on the Himalayas, in Champawat District, Uttrakhand, called the Advaita Ashrama. These monasteries were meant to receive and train young men who would eventually become sannyasis (religious ascetic) of the Ramakrishna Mission, and to give them a training for their work. The same year the philanthropic activity was started and relief of the famine was carried out. Later drive to Kolkata airport to board flight for Delhi. days.heading: ARRIVE DELHI
days.body: Meeting and assistance upon arrival at Delhi International Airport transfer to hotel in Delhi. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Delhi. Delhi – Where Centuries of History Meet the Pulse of Modern India: Few capital cities in the world possess a history as rich, captivating, and enduring as Delhi, the timeless capital of India. For over a millennium, this legendary city has stood at the crossroads of empires, drawing successive dynasties—including the Mongols, Turks, Persians, Afghans, Mughals, and the British—each leaving behind an extraordinary architectural, cultural, and historical legacy that continues to define the city's unique character. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Delhi

days.heading: DELHI
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for Delhi Sightseeing – A Journey Through the Capital’s Heritage The experience then takes you into the vibrant heart of Old Delhi, beginning with a visit to the historic Jama Masjid, commissioned in the 17th century by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Its impressive courtyards, soaring minarets, and red sandstone and marble architecture make it one of the finest examples of Mughal religious architecture in the city. Continue to Chandni Chowk, the historic commercial heart of Old Delhi, where narrow lanes, colourful markets, traditional shops, street-food stalls, and the lively rhythm of everyday life create an unmistakably authentic Delhi experience. A drive past the magnificent Red Fort, with a brief photo stop, offers a glimpse of another great symbol of the Mughal era. Conclude the sightseeing at Raj Ghat, the serene memorial marking the cremation site of Mahatma Gandhi. Set amidst peaceful landscaped gardens, it provides a quiet and reflective conclusion to a day spent discovering Delhi’s remarkable history and heritage Afternoon proceed for an astonishing and beautiful fountain show at Akshardha Temple Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Delhi

Jaisalmer – The Golden City of the Thar: The captivating city of Jaisalmer, founded in 1156 AD by Prince Jaisal, rises like a golden jewel from the vast expanse of the Thar Desert. Often celebrated as the “Golden City,” Jaisalmer derives its distinctive character from the warm honey-gold hue of its yellow sandstone architecture, which glows magnificently as the setting sun bathes its ancient walls in a luminous golden light. Encircled by crenellated fortifications and threaded with narrow, atmospheric lanes, the old city possesses an extraordinary medieval charm. Exquisitely carved façades, ornate balconies, finely detailed windows and magnificent sandstone buildings reveal the exceptional craftsmanship that has shaped Jaisalmer through the centuries. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Jaisalmer

days.heading: JAISALMER – POKHARAN – JODHPUR (272Kms, 04Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Jodhpur enroot visiting Pokhran Fort, also known as Balagarh Fort, a distinguished Rajput stronghold rising amidst the stark and captivating landscapes of the Thar Desert. Built in the 14th century by Rao Maldeo, the fort is an impressive example of traditional Rajput architecture, characterised by its imposing sandstone walls, fortified gateways and finely carved architectural details. Constructed as both a fortress and royal residence, Pokhran Fort reflects the remarkable ability of Rajput architects to combine military strength with the elegance and comforts of royal living. Its architecture was thoughtfully adapted to the demanding desert environment, with carefully planned courtyards, shaded spaces and thick sandstone walls providing protection from the harsh climate. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Jodhpur

days.heading: JODHPUR – RANAKPUR – UDAIPUR (262Kms, 05Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Jodhpur enroot visiting Ranakpur – A Marble Masterpiece of Jain Architecture: Nestled amidst the tranquil Aravalli Hills, approximately 90 km from Udaipur, Ranakpur is home to one of India’s most magnificent Jain temple complexes and one of the finest expressions of medieval western Indian temple architecture. Dating from the 15th century, the complex is centred around the spectacular Chaumukha Temple, dedicated to Adinath, the first Tirthankara of Jainism. Built almost entirely in beautifully worked marble, the temple is a masterpiece of intricate craftsmanship. Its walls, pillars and domes are adorned with exquisite carvings depicting mythological figures, floral patterns, geometric motifs and finely detailed ornamental designs. The temple is particularly renowned for its 1,444 intricately carved marble pillars, each uniquely designed, creating an extraordinary interplay of light, shadow and symmetry throughout the vast interior. Continue drive to Udaipur. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Udaipur. Udaipur – The Romantic Soul of Rajasthan: Nestled amidst the undulating Aravalli Hills of southern Rajasthan, Udaipur is one of India's most enchanting cities and is widely regarded as one of the country's most romantic destinations. With its shimmering lakes, magnificent marble palaces, beautifully landscaped gardens and lush green hills, the city presents a picture of timeless elegance and has earned the evocative title of “Venice of the East.” Founded by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1568, Udaipur was conceived as a traditionally planned and fortified city, with imposing palaces, ornate temples, elegant havelis and defensive structures woven into its landscape. The city's architecture reflects the grandeur and sophistication of the Mewar dynasty, while its lakes and surrounding hills lend it an unmistakable sense of tranquillity. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Udaipur

days.heading: UDAIPUR
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for sightseeing tour of Udaipur City Tour – Palaces, Temples & Artistic Heritage: Begin your half-day sightseeing tour of Udaipur with a visit to the magnificent City Palace and Museum, an extraordinary complex rising majestically above the shores of Lake Pichola. Considered one of the largest palace complexes in India, it represents a harmonious fusion of Rajput architectural traditions and Mughal influences. Explore its ornate courtyards, grand halls, balconies and richly decorated chambers, while the museum offers fascinating insights into the splendour and lifestyle of the former Mewar rulers. Continue to the beautiful Jagdish Temple, an impressive 17th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Its towering structure and intricate stone carvings make it one of Udaipur's most significant religious and architectural landmarks. Take a scenic drive around Fateh Sagar Lake, one of Udaipur's most picturesque lakes, framed by the Aravalli Hills and surrounded by a tranquil landscape. The drive offers wonderful views of the water and the city's elegant lakeside setting. Visit Saheliyon-ki-Bari, meaning the “Garden of the Maids of Honour,” a graceful ornamental garden created as a retreat for the royal ladies. Beautiful fountains, marble kiosks, lotus pools, manicured lawns and shady walkways create an atmosphere of serenity and refinement, offering a glimpse into the leisure and elegance of the Mewar court. Conclude the sightseeing with a visit to the Bharatiya Lok Kala Mandal, also known as the Folk Art Museum, where an engaging collection of traditional Rajasthani folk art, costumes, puppets, masks, musical instruments and decorative crafts celebrates the vibrant cultural traditions of the region. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Udaipur

Nestled within a narrow valley and surrounded by the rugged Aravalli landscape, the town retains an unmistakable medieval charm, with its winding lanes, historic architecture and tranquil ambience.
