Agra – The Mughal City of Eternal Grandeur: Although Agra’s history stretches back centuries, the city rose to particular prominence during the reign of the Afghan ruler Sikandar Lodi, who established it as the capital of his empire. A defining chapter in Agra’s history began in 1526, when the Mughal Emperor Babur conquered the city and began shaping its architectural and cultural character. Over the following centuries, Agra witnessed the extraordinary splendour of the Mughal Empire under three of its most celebrated rulers—Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan. Their reigns transformed Agra into a magnificent centre of imperial power, artistic refinement, architecture and craftsmanship. The city flourished with grand forts, elegant palaces, exquisite gardens and monumental structures, leaving behind an architectural legacy that continues to define Agra’s identity today. days.heading: ARRIVAL – CHENNAI
days.body: Upon arrival at Chennai International Airport, meet and receive assistance before transferring to your hotel. Check in and relax after your journey. Overnight stay in Chennai

days.heading: CHENNAI – KANCHIPURAM – MAHABALIPURAM (150 km / 4 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, embark on a guided sightseeing tour of Chennai. Visit the Government Museum to admire the renowned bronze gallery showcasing exquisite Chola art. Drive through the vibrant flower and fruit markets, past the Indo-Saracenic High Court, and the Fort Museum housing colonial-era memorabilia. Continue to Marina Beach, one of the longest urban beaches in the world. Visit San Thome Cathedral, believed to enshrine the relics of St. Thomas the Apostle, Kapaleeshwara Temple, and the Snake Park. Later, drive towards Mahabalipuram, stopping en route at Kanchipuram, one of India’s seven sacred cities. Dating back to the early Chola period (2nd century), Kanchipuram was once home to over 1,000 temples, of which about 200 remain. Visit the 7th-century Kailasanatha Temple, the beautifully sculpted Varadaraja Temple with its 96-pillared hall, Ekambareswarar Temple, and Vaikuntha Perumal Temple. The town is also renowned for its fine silk weaving tradition. Continue to Mahabalipuram. Upon arrival, check in at the hotel. Overnight stay in Mahabalipuram

days.heading: MAHABALIPURAM – PONDICHERRY (95 km / 2 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, proceed for sightseeing in Mahabalipuram, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore its remarkable rock-cut and monolithic monuments, including cave temples, rathas, mandapams, and sculpted relief panels dating from the 7th–8th centuries. Highlights include the Shore Temple, Arjuna’s Penance, and the Five Rathas, depicting scenes from Hindu mythology and daily life. Later, drive to Pondicherry. Check in upon arrival. In the afternoon, visit the Sri Aurobindo Ashram, founded in 1926 as a spiritual community blending yoga and modern thought. Also visit the Pondicherry Museum, showcasing archaeological artifacts and French colonial memorabilia, and the Sacred Heart Church, noted for its Gothic architecture and stained-glass windows. Overnight stay in Pondicherry

days.heading: PONDICHERRY – TANJORE (173 km / 2 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, drive to Tanjore and check in at your hotel. The remainder of the day is free for leisure or exploring the surroundings. Overnight stay in Tanjore

days.heading: TANJORE
days.body: After breakfast, visit the iconic Brihadeeswara (Brahadeeswara) Temple, an 11th-century architectural marvel built entirely of granite. Admire its towering vimana crowned with a single 80-ton granite dome, an engineering feat achieved using a 6-kilometre ramp. Overnight stay in Tanjore

days.heading: TANJORE – RAMESHWARAM (248 km / 04 hr)
days.body: After breakfast, drive to Rameshwaram and check in at the hotel. Rest of the day free for relaxation / explore surrounding Overnight stay in Rameshwaram

days.heading: RAMESHWARAM
days.body: After breakfast, proceed for a full-day sightseeing tour. Visit the sacred Ramanathaswamy Temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva. Renowned for its magnificent gopurams, intricately carved pillars, longest temple corridors in India, and a towering Nandi statue, the temple is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture and spiritual devotion. Continue to Dhanushkodi Beach, located at the confluence of the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean. Steeped in Ramayana legends, it is believed to be the site where Lord Rama initiated the construction of the bridge to Lanka. The pristine white sands, turquoise waters, and haunting ruins create a powerful and unforgettable atmosphere. Visit Agni Theertham, the sacred seashore opposite the Ramanathaswamy Temple. According to legend, Lord Agni bathed here to absolve himself after testifying to Goddess Sita’s purity. A holy dip here is believed to cleanse sins and bestow spiritual merit. Overnight stay in Rameshwaram

days.heading: RAMESHWARAM – KANYAKUMARI (308 km / 6 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, drive to Kanyakumari, the southernmost tip of mainland India. Upon arrival, check in at the hotel. Located at the confluence of the Indian Ocean, Arabian Sea, and Bay of Bengal, Kanyakumari is a revered pilgrimage destination dedicated to Goddess Kanya Devi. Visit the Vivekananda Rock Memorial, built in honor of Swami Vivekananda. Kanyakumari is uniquely famous for witnessing both sunset and moonrise on full-moon evenings. Overnight stay in Kanyakumari

days.heading: KANYAKUMARI – MADURAI (245 km / 4 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, drive to Madurai and check in. In the afternoon, visit the magnificent Meenakshi Amman Temple, a jewel of Dravidian architecture adorned with towering gopurams covered in vibrant sculptures. Also visit the Tirumalai Nayak Palace, a 17th-century Indo-Saracenic structure renowned for its grand arches and decorative stucco work. Overnight stay in Madurai

days.heading: MADURAI – COIMBATORE (217 km / 4 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, drive to Coimbatore and check in at hotel in Coimbatore. In the afternoon, visit the Sri Svetambara Vimalanthar Jain Temple, dedicated to Lord Vimalanatha, known for its serene atmosphere and spiritual simplicity. Continue to St. Michael Xavier Church in Big Bazaar, one of the city’s oldest churches, admired for its graceful architecture. Also visit the historic Athar Jamid Mosque on Oppalamara Street, an important Islamic landmark reflecting Coimbatore’s multicultural heritage. Overnight stay in Coimbatore

days.heading: COIMBATORE – OOTY (87 km / 3 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, drive to the scenic hill station of Ooty. Upon arrival, check in at the hotel. The rest of the day is free for leisure or exploring the surroundings. Overnight stay in Ooty

days.heading: OOTY
days.body: After breakfast, enjoy a sightseeing tour of Ooty. Visit the Botanical Gardens established in 1848, home to over 1,000 plant species and a 200-million-year-old fossilized tree trunk. Visit Ooty Lake for boating and proceed to Doddabetta Peak, the highest point in the Nilgiri Hills, offering panoramic views. Overnight stay in Ooty

days.heading: OOTY – MYSORE (269 km / 7 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, drive to Mysore. Upon arrival, check in at the hotel. The rest of the day is free for relaxation or local exploration. Overnight stay in Mysore

days.heading: MYSORE – BANGALORE (142 km / 2 hrs)
days.body: After breakfast, visit the grand Mysore Palace, built in 1911–12, a stunning blend of Hindu and Saracenic architectural styles. Visit the art gallery and proceed to Chamundi Hill to see the Chamundeshwari Temple and enjoy panoramic views of Mysore. En route, view the massive monolithic Nandi Bull statue carved in 1659. Later, drive to Bangalore and check in at the hotel. Overnight stay in Bangalore

days.heading: ARRIVAL CHENNAI
days.body: Meeting and assistance upon arrival at Chennai International Airport and transfer to the hotel. Upon arrival, check in at hotel in Chennai. Afternoon proceed for half day Chennai Sightseeing – A Glimpse into Tamil Nadu’s Heritage: Begin your exploration of Chennai with a visit to the Government Museum, renowned for its remarkable collection of South Indian art and antiquities. Admire the exceptional Bronze Gallery, featuring a superb collection of exquisite Chola bronzes that beautifully reflect the artistic mastery, craftsmanship, and spiritual traditions of the Chola dynasty. Continue with a drive through the vibrant flower and fruit markets, offering a colourful glimpse into the everyday rhythm of Chennai. Proceed past the magnificent Madras High Court, an impressive landmark built in the distinctive Indo-Saracenic architectural style, showcasing the city’s rich colonial heritage. Continue to Fort St. George and visit the Fort Museum, which houses an interesting collection of colonial memorabilia, historic artefacts, weapons, uniforms, and other exhibits that bring Chennai’s colonial past vividly to life. Drive along Marina Beach, one of Chennai’s most celebrated landmarks and among the longest urban beaches in the world. Take in the refreshing sea breeze and observe the lively atmosphere along the beachfront, where local life unfolds against the vast expanse of the Bay of Bengal. Continue to the San Thome Cathedral, an elegant neo-Gothic basilica traditionally associated with the final resting place of St. Thomas the Apostle, offering an intriguing connection between Chennai and the early Christian history of India. The sightseeing continues with a visit to the magnificent Kapaleeshwarar Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva and celebrated for its vibrant Dravidian architecture, intricately sculpted gopuram, and deeply rooted religious traditions. Conclude the tour with a visit to the Guindy Snake Park, home to a fascinating variety of reptiles and an interesting insight into India’s diverse wildlife. Together, these experiences reveal the many facets of Chennai—from Chola artistry and Dravidian spirituality to colonial architecture, vibrant markets, Christian heritage, and coastal charm, offering an enriching introduction to the cultural character of Tamil Nadu. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel in Chennai

days.heading: DELHI – VARANASI (6E 2571 – 10:30 / 11:45 Hrs)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to airport to board flight for Varanasi. Meeting and assistance upon arrival at Varanasi airport and transfer to hotel in Varanasi. Varanasi, often revered as the spiritual capital of India, is one of the world’s oldest living cities—a timeless destination where faith, philosophy, culture, and tradition flow as seamlessly as the sacred Ganges that graces its shores. Nestled along the banks of the holy river in Uttar Pradesh, this ancient city is a profound confluence of devotion and heritage, drawing pilgrims, scholars, and travelers from across the globe. Steeped in mythology and history, Varanasi is believed to have been founded by Lord Shiva himself, making it one of the most sacred centers of Hindu belief. For millennia, seekers have journeyed here in pursuit of spiritual awakening, liberation (moksha), and divine blessings. The city’s iconic ghats—stone steps descending to the river—serve as the focal point of daily rituals, sacred ceremonies, and the eternal rhythm of life and death that defines its character. Evening wittness aarti ceremony on river Ganges. The Ganga Aarti in Varanasi is one of India’s most captivating and spiritually uplifting rituals, performed every evening on the sacred banks of the River Ganges. This grand ceremony is a devotional offering to Mother Ganga, revered in Hindu belief as a goddess who purifies the soul and washes away sins. The most prominent and widely attended Aarti takes place at Dashashwamedh Ghat, where a group of young priests dressed in traditional saffron and cream attire perform the ritual in perfect synchronization. As dusk settles over the river, the atmosphere transforms into a divine spectacle of rhythmic chants, resonating temple bells, conch shells, and the fragrance of incense. The ceremony begins with Vedic mantras and devotional hymns, followed by the priests holding large multi-tiered brass lamps blazing with fire. In graceful, circular movements, they offer light to the river while facing the sacred waters. The flames illuminate the twilight sky, reflecting beautifully on the flowing Ganges, creating an ethereal and unforgettable sight. Overnight stay at hotel in Varanasi

days.heading: VARANASI – BODHGAYA (255 Kms , 05 Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Bodhgaya. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Bodhgaya. The serene village of Bodh Gaya, situated on the tranquil banks of the Niranjana River and approximately 16 km from Gaya, stands as one of the most sacred Buddhist pilgrimage centres in the world. It was here that Prince Siddhartha attained Supreme Enlightenment and became the Buddha while meditating beneath the revered Bodhi Tree. At the heart of Bodhgaya lies the magnificent Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that marks the exact spot of enlightenment. Within the temple complex stands the sacred Bodhi Tree, whose present sapling is believed to be a direct descendant of the original tree under which enlightenment was attained. Pilgrims from across the globe gather here for meditation and prayer, enveloping the surroundings in an atmosphere of deep spiritual reverence and peace. Overnight stay at hotel in Bodhgaya.

days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Dharamshala. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Dharamshala. Nestled in the serene Kangra Valley against the dramatic backdrop of the Dhauladhar mountain range, Dharamshala is one of Himachal Pradesh’s most picturesque hill destinations. Renowned for its natural beauty, spiritual ambiance, and Tibetan cultural influence, the town offers a refreshing blend of tranquility and vibrant heritage. Divided into Lower Dharamshala and Upper Dharamshala (McLeod Ganj), the area gained international prominence as the residence of Dalai Lama and the seat of the Tibetan Government-in-Exile. This has transformed Dharamshala into a significant center of Tibetan Buddhism, attracting spiritual seekers and travelers from across the globe. Overnight stay at hotel in Dharamshala

days.heading: DHARAMSHALA – SHIMLA (232 Kms, 06 Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Shimla. Upon arrival check in at Shimla. Fondly referred to by the British as the “Queen of Hill Stations,” Shimla is one of India’s most charming mountain retreats. Nestled in the northwestern Himalayas at an elevation of approximately 7,238 feet, it once served as the summer capital of British India and today stands as the capital of Himachal Pradesh. The name Shimla is derived from “Shyamala,” another name for Goddess Kali, whose temple once stood amidst the dense forests covering Jakhu Hill in the early 19th century. Over time, the British adapted the name to “Shimla,” and the town gradually evolved into a favored colonial escape from the plains’ summer heat. Spread across nearly 18 square kilometers, Shimla is enveloped by picturesque forests of pine, deodar, oak, and rhododendron. Its colonial-era architecture, scenic promenades, and cool mountain air lend the city a timeless appeal. Landmarks such as the Viceregal Lodge, Christ Church, and the bustling Mall Road reflect its rich historical legacy. Overnight stay at hotel in Shimla

days.heading: SHIMLA
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for sightseeing tour of Shimla. Begin with a leisurely stroll along The Mall Road, the vibrant heart of Shimla, lined with colonial-era buildings, cafés, boutiques, and souvenir shops. Nearby stands the iconic Christ Church, one of the oldest churches in North India, known for its neo-Gothic architecture and beautiful stained-glass windows. Visit the historic Viceregal Lodge (also known as Rashtrapati Niwas), a grand colonial structure that once served as the residence of the British Viceroy. Surrounded by manicured gardens, the building reflects remarkable Scottish baronial architecture and played a key role during India’s independence era. Proceed to Jakhu Temple, situated atop Jakhu Hill—the highest point in Shimla. Dedicated to Lord Hanuman, the temple offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. Nature lovers can explore The Ridge, an open space offering spectacular sunset views, or take a scenic drive to Kufri, a nearby hill spot known for its natural beauty and adventure activities. Overnight stay at hotel in Shimla

days.heading: SHIMLA – CHANDIGARH (109 Kms, 02 Hrs drive)
days.body: Morning after breakfast drive to Chandigarh. Upon arrival check in at hotel in Chandigarh. Chandigarh, the joint capital of Punjab and Haryana, stands apart as one of India’s most meticulously planned and modern cities. Designed by the renowned French architect Le Corbusier, the city represents a bold experiment in urban planning and contemporary architecture in post-independence India. Unlike the organically evolved cities of the country, Chandigarh was carefully structured into well-defined sectors, each functioning as a self-sufficient neighborhood. Broad tree-lined boulevards, organized layouts, landscaped gardens, and modernist government buildings give the city a distinctive character and an overall air of order and prosperity. The architectural landmarks of the Capitol Complex, geometric forms, and open spaces reflect Le Corbusier’s vision of a progressive India. Combined with its clean environment and abundant green spaces, Chandigarh offers a refreshing contrast to traditional Indian cityscapes—making it a symbol of modern urban design and civic planning in the country. Rest of the day free for relaxation / explore surroundings Overnight stay at hotel in Chandigarh

days.heading: CHANDIGARH
days.body: Morning after breakfast enjoy a half-day tour of Chandigarh, a city celebrated for its modern architecture and thoughtfully planned layout. Begin with a visit to the iconic Capitol Complex, which houses the imposing Secretariat Building, the striking Punjab and Haryana Legislative Assembly, and the multi-pillared Punjab and Haryana High Court. Designed by the visionary architect Le Corbusier, these monumental structures exemplify bold modernist design and symbolize India’s progressive spirit after independence. Continue to the State Library and Panjab University campus, both reflecting the city’s emphasis on education and cultural development. Later, unwind amidst nature at the renowned Zakir Hussain Rose Garden, home to more than 1,500 varieties of roses and one of Asia’s largest rose gardens. Stroll through its beautifully landscaped lawns and vibrant floral displays. Also visit the Botanical Garden, a tranquil retreat showcasing diverse plant species, before concluding your tour at the picturesque Sukhna Lake. This serene man-made lake, set against the backdrop of the Shivalik Hills, offers a peaceful environment ideal for leisurely walks and scenic views. Overnight stay at hotel in Chandigarh

Perhaps no other capital city in the world is as deeply steeped in history and legend as Delhi, the heart of India. For centuries, it stood as a powerful magnet for invaders and emperors—drawing Mongols, Turks, Persians, Afghans, Mughals, and eventually the British. Each dynasty left behind an indelible imprint, contributing to the city’s glorious yet turbulent past. Such was the fascination with Delhi that despite being abandoned and rebuilt multiple times, its rulers continually returned, reconstructing it at least seven times over the centuries. From ancient fortified cities to grand imperial capitals, Delhi evolved as a symbol of authority, ambition, and resilience. Today, the twin cities of Old and New Delhi present a captivating contrast. Old Delhi echoes with the charm of narrow lanes, bustling bazaars, and Mughal-era monuments, while New Delhi reflects colonial grandeur and modern governance with its wide boulevards and stately buildings. Together, they form the cultural and political nucleus of the world’s largest democracy. Overnight stay at hotel in Delhi

days.body: After breakfast, embark on a guided sightseeing tour of Delhi. New Delhi is built in a typically British colonial style with tree-lined avenues and colonial bungalows. See the Laxminarayan Temple, a modern Hindu temple, and India Gate, the 42 m high War Memorial Arch. days.heading: 10 MAR’27 | AGRA
days.body: Morning after breakfast proceed for sightseeing tour of Agra visiting Taj Mahal: Shahjahan, who was a passionate builder, now decided to erect a memorial marble that the world would never forget. The site was also chosen because it was located on a bend in the river, and so could be seen from Shahjahan's personal palace in Agra Fort, further upstream. The construction of the Taj Mahal started in 1631. It took 20,000 artisans 22 years to complete this poignant mauseoleum that blends subtlety with grandeur, and a massive overall design with immaculately intricate execution. Agra Fort: The construction of the Agra Fort was begun by Emperor Akbar in 1565. Its massive walls stretch for 2½ km and are surrounded by a moat over 10 metres wide. The fort is really a city within a city, which embraces the Moti Masjid, the Diwan-i-Am or the Hall of Public Audiences, the Diwan-i-Khas or the Hall of Private Audiences, the Octagonal Tower, Jehangir’s Palace and many more monuments. Itmad-Ud-Daula: This tomb was built in 1622 for Ghiyas Beg, father of Empress Noor-Jahan, the wife of Emperor Jahangir. It is beautifully conceived in white marble, mosaic and lattice and set a precedent as the first Mughal building to be faced with white marble inlaid with contrasting stones. Sometimes also called ‘Baby Taj’, it is small, intimate and has a gentle serenity Overnight stay in Agra hotel

Planned by Viceroy Curzon and referred to both as Curzon’s Folly and the British Taj Mahal it is a museum housing Imperial memorabilia. Drive past the Howrah Bridge, one of the largest cantilever bridges in the world, the Dalhousie Square, Fort Williams, the secretariat building and the Old Court House Street. Also visit the 16 hectare Zoological gardens. Overnight stay in Kolkata hotel
